mixed_loading_7_5_2.basis: every pair of lines (one load in one transport unit) against the 7.5.2.1 table by the labels of Table A column (5); Class 1 pairs against the 7.5.2.2 table by the compatibility group of column (3b)

pairs.note: note a — not met (UN 0336 is 1.4G): "Mixed loading permitted with 1.4S substances and articles." (7.5.2.1 table, note a, Vol. II p. 602)

source_ref.quote: unless mixed loading is permitted according to the following Table based on the danger labels they bear.

notes: Basis: the lines of one consignment object are one load in one transport unit, so every pair of lines is read as packages loaded together in the same vehicle or container (7.5.2.1).

Every label of Table A column (5) counts, subsidiary labels included (7.5.2.1: the table is read "based on the danger labels they bear"); a line bearing 4.1 and 1 (or 5.2 and 1) is read under the combined heading the table prints for it. Column (6) special provisions may change the labels (3.2.1 column (5) NOTE) — not applied.

7.5.2.3: "no account shall be taken of substances contained in closed containers with complete sides." (7.5.2.3, Vol. II p. 603) — but the prohibitions for labels 1, 1.4, 1.5 or 1.6 (7.5.2.1) and between compatibility groups (7.5.2.2) still apply to goods in a container on the same vehicle, and every prohibition of the 7.5.2.1 table involves such a label: a closed container does not lift any prohibition found here.
7.5.2.1 NOTE 1: "separate transport documents shall be drawn up for consignments that cannot be loaded together" (7.5.2.1 NOTE 1, Vol. II p. 602).
1.1.3.6.2: the provisions a 1.1.3.6 load is carried without name, in Chapter 7.5, only CV1 of 7.5.11 — 7.5.2 and 7.5.4 still apply, so this verdict stands under the relief.
